citation: Duncan, T., Moeller, B., Schoeneberger, J., & Hitchcock, J. (2018). Assessing the impact of the Math for All professional development program on elementary school teachers and their students. New York, NY: Education Development Center. (IES Grant No. R305A140488).
report_number: EDC Math for All Year 1 study brief (IES Grant R305A140488); WWC study ID 86097
design: Two-year cluster RCT; school-level random assignment; 32 Chicago Public Schools randomized (16 MFA / 16 BAU) in Oct 2015; grades 4-5 general & special education teachers (~96) and ~1,500 students; outcome = student mathematics achievement (NWEA MAP); Year 1 (implementation year, 2015-2016) results are causally valid (cluster sample intact); Year 2 excluded due to attrition (would not meet WWC standards).
problems: The report does NOT print impact SEs or design-effect ICCs; it reports a Hedges' g and a p-value (of the treatment indicator) for each contrast, derived from HGLM/ANCOVA-adjusted means. impact_se and g_var were therefore back-derived from the reported two-tailed p-value via the inverse normal (z = invNorm(1 - p/2); SE = |g| / z), matching the precision of the report's own multilevel model (this is preferable to the naive independent-student variance formula, which would mis-state variance for this clustered design). g values are taken verbatim from the report (Hedges' g, pretest/covariate-adjusted, standardized via the report's 'Statistical Adjustment'); they are NOT recomputed from means/SDs. No ICC reported -> icc left null per spec (never guess). The school-level (Exhibit 19) and student-level (Exhibit 20) analyses cover the SAME full sample via two different analytic approaches (cluster-aggregated vs student-level); to avoid double-counting, the student-level full-sample estimate is marked outcome_role=primary and the school-level aggregate is marked outcome_role=composite. Grade-4 and Grade-5 rows are moderator subgroups (is_full_sample=false). For each contrast the report gives an unimputed and (except school-level) a multiply-imputed version; the imputed estimate is used as the primary g where available (report's main analysis used multiple imputation accounting for the teacher/student-within-school multilevel structure), with the unimputed value recorded in notes. n_t/n_c for imputed analyses are the per-imputation analytic sample sizes (total across 20 imputations divided by 20). Year 2 (two-year) student impacts could not be validly estimated by the authors (sample loss) and are not extracted.

effect_sizes.arm_label: Math for All PD (~50 hrs: 5 one-day workshops + classroom-based assignments; lesson study, collaborative planning, peer coaching, video-case analysis, formative assessment) vs business-as-usual control
effect_sizes.test_name: NWEA Measures of Academic Progress (MAP) mathematics, RIT scale (student-level analysis)
effect_sizes.timepoint: post, Spring 2016 (end of Year 1 / implementation year)
effect_sizes.g_method: Hedges' g reported verbatim by the authors (imputed student-level analysis), computed from pretest/covariate-adjusted posttest means of a 2-level model (students nested in schools; pretest, treatment, economically-disadvantaged, white, ELL fixed effects + random school intercept), standardized via the report's 'Statistical Adjustment' (baseline-equivalence g=0.20). g_se/g_var back-derived from the reported two-tailed p=0.187: SE = |g|/invNorm(1-p/2) = 0.14/1.319 = 0.1061; g_var = SE^2.
effect_sizes.page_ref: p. 11 (RQ4 narrative); Exhibit 11 (summary, printed p. 28); Exhibit 20 (NWEA Student-Level, printed p. 37)
effect_sizes.notes: Full-sample student-level estimate, multiply-imputed (20 imputations; reported per-imputation n = 451 MFA, 483 BAU; total 9,020 MFA / 9,660 BAU rows). Not statistically significant (p=0.187). Unimputed counterpart (Exhibit 20): adj posttest MFA 214.010 (SD 14.514), BAU 212.470 (SD 14.409), n=423 MFA / 458 BAU, Hedges' g = 0.106, p=0.394. NWEA MAP is an independent/standardized adaptive assessment (Exhibit 10). Pretest = Spring 2015 MAP; posttest = Spring 2016 MAP.

effect_sizes.test_name: NWEA Measures of Academic Progress (MAP) mathematics, RIT scale (school-level / cluster-aggregated analysis)

effect_sizes.g_method: Hedges' g reported verbatim by the authors (school-level / cluster-aggregated analysis), computed from pretest-adjusted school-mean posttest scores (32 school-level units), standardized via the report's 'Statistical Adjustment' (baseline-equivalence g=0.10). g_se/g_var back-derived from the reported two-tailed p=0.086: SE = |g|/invNorm(1-p/2) = 0.327/1.717 = 0.1905; g_var = SE^2.
effect_sizes.page_ref: p. 11 (RQ4 narrative); Exhibit 11 (summary, printed p. 28); Exhibit 19 (NWEA School-Level, printed p. 36)
effect_sizes.notes: Same full sample as the student-level row, aggregated to the 32 school clusters (includes ALL grade 4 & 5 students at the study schools, even those of nonparticipating teachers, so this aggregate DILUTES the treatment effect). Marked outcome_role=composite so central merge logic treats it as the cluster aggregate of the student-level full-sample outcome and does not double-count it. Not statistically significant (p=0.086), attributed by authors to small unit sample (32 schools). mean_t/mean_c/sd_t/sd_c here are school-level adjusted means and SDs. Unadjusted posttest school means: MFA 212.923, BAU 210.634. No imputed version (Exhibit 11 lists N/A for imputed school-level).

effect_sizes.notes: Grade-4 moderator subgroup; multiply-imputed (per-imputation n = 261 MFA / 262 BAU; totals 5,220 / 5,240). Statistically significant in the imputed analysis (p=0.028) - the only significant student-achievement result. Unimputed grade-4 (Exhibit 21): adj posttest MFA 211.520 (SD 14.149), BAU 208.750 (SD 13.053), n=242 MFA / 247 BAU, Hedges' g = 0.203, p=0.159 (not significant). Subgroup (not full sample) per spec because it is a non-randomised grade-level subset.

effect_sizes.notes: Grade-5 moderator subgroup; multiply-imputed (per-imputation n = 190 MFA / 221 BAU; totals 3,800 / 4,420). Negative g = slightly favors control; not statistically significant (p=0.739). Unimputed grade-5 (Exhibit 22): adj posttest MFA 217.080 (SD 14.672), BAU 217.880 (SD 14.263), n=181 MFA / 211 BAU, Hedges' g = -0.055, p=0.649. Subgroup (not full sample) per spec. Note: derived SE is unstable because p is near 1 and g is near 0; the SE here should be treated as approximate.
